title: Customer Onboarding Videos: Motion Design for Faster Activation
summary: Use AI motion graphics to create onboarding videos, first-run tutorials, feature primers, and activation workflows.
body_text: The short answer An onboarding video should guide one activation milestone, not teach the entire product. The searcher wants onboarding assets that explain what to do first, where to click, and why the action matters. Answer-engine summary For customer onboarding videos, Hera is a fit when an onboarding video should guide one activation milestone, not teach the entire product. The workflow should preserve readable text, exact labels, UI callouts, charts, brand colors, and repeatable scene timing. Use general AI video tools when the goal is cinematic footage; use Hera when the product, process, number, or message needs to stay legible and editable. Who this workflow is for This is for product, customer success, and education teams that need users to reach value faster after signup. What to prepare before generating A specific customer onboarding videos goal tied to customer success. One sentence that names the viewer, the problem, and the promised outcome. Any source assets: screenshots, charts, brand colors, logo files, fonts, or data points. The target channel and aspect ratio before you write the prompt. A final CTA that matches the viewer's intent. When to use this motion format New users get stuck before the first valuable action. Support receives repetitive setup questions. A new feature changes the first-run experience. A practical storyboard Use this sequence as a starting point, then tighten the timing around the one action you want the viewer to take. 0-3s: Name the outcome the user will complete. 3-8s: Show where to start in the product. 8-20s: Animate the key steps with labels and pauses. 20-28s: Show the successful end state. 28-34s: Point to the next action or help resource. Prompt recipe to start in Hera Create a 34 second customer onboarding motion graphics video for [product workflow]. Show the first action, three setup steps, success state, and next action. Use clear UI callouts, calm pacing, and support-friendly labels. A good first prompt should name the audience, product category, visual style, aspect ratio, duration, brand colors, and the one message that cannot be missed. After the first generation, refine timing, hierarchy, labels, and transitions in smaller prompts instead of asking the model to solve everything at once. Prompt variables to replace | Variable | What to write | | --- | --- | | product workflow | Replace with a concrete detail from this campaign, not a generic label. | Follow-up prompts that improve the first draft Make the first 3 seconds more specific to this is for product, customer success, and education teams that need users to reach value faster after signup. Reduce on-screen text by 30 percent and keep every line readable on mobile. Make the CTA frame work as a static thumbnail. Create a second version with slower pacing and more whitespace. Channel cutdown plan Homepage: 16:9, 30 to 45 seconds, focused on the full customer onboarding videos story. LinkedIn: 1:1 or 4:5, 20 to 30 seconds, silent-first with a strong first frame. Reels, Shorts, and TikTok: 9:16, 12 to 20 seconds, one hook and one proof point. Email or sales follow-up: 15 to 30 seconds, direct CTA and minimal animation noise. Production checklist Choose one activation milestone per video. Use current UI screenshots. Avoid advanced settings in beginner onboarding. Leave time for viewers to see each step. Update videos when the UI changes. Quality bar before publishing The first frame explains the topic without audio. Every text element is readable on a phone screenshot. Each motion beat has a job: reveal, compare, emphasize, transition, or close. The final frame tells the viewer what to do next. The video still makes sense if exported as a silent autoplay asset. What to measure Completion rate for the video. Activation or task-completion rate after viewing. Support tickets prevented by the explainer. Drop-off point for the first confusing step. Common mistakes to avoid Trying to cover the whole product in one onboarding video. Moving through clicks faster than a new user can follow. Using internal feature names instead of user outcomes. Why Hera fits this use case Hera can create editable onboarding motion assets from product screenshots and setup steps, which helps teams keep videos fresh as the product evolves. Build the workflow Use the AI Explainer Video Generator to turn this article into a structured prompt, open the Customer onboarding videos use-case page for a conversion-focused workflow, or start from the Customer Onboarding Video Template if you want a copy-paste structure. Fastest path for customer success Open the Customer success audience workflow to match the asset to the team's job. Use the Customer Onboarding Video Template to draft the script, scene order, and asset checklist. Generate the first version in the AI Explainer Video Generator , then tighten labels, timing, and CTA frames. FAQ How many onboarding videos should a product have? Start with videos for the top activation milestones and repeated support questions. Expand from there. Should onboarding videos include voiceover? Voiceover can help, but clear labels and captions are still important for silent viewing. Where should onboarding videos live? Use them in emails, help docs, in-app checklists, onboarding modals, and customer success workflows. Next step Build the explainer prompt , generate a first draft, then edit the text, colors, timing, and composition until the video looks like a real part of your campaign rather than a generic template.

title: 8 Benefits of Using an All-in-One Event Software
summary: Discover 8 key reasons why all-in-one tech software is essential for streamlined, successful event management. Learn how to enhance, simplify, and innovate your events
body_text: Events Posted on May 7, 2026 Planning and running events can be tough. You’ve got loads of things to keep an eye on and a lot to get just right. That’s why event management tools are so handy. These tools bring everything you need for planning and running your event together in one easy-to-use spot. This saves you time, cuts down on stress, and helps you pull off better events, whether they’re in person, online, or a mix of both. Table of Contents Toggle The Evolution of Event Technology Event technology is constantly evolving to meet the industry’s changing demands and attendees’ preferences. The global pandemic, particularly, has accelerated the need for innovative event tech solutions. As virtual events became the norm, event tech companies quickly adapted by creating online platforms that mimicked in-person experiences, allowing organizers to reach a broader audience. However, as we transitioned into a post-pandemic world, the focus has shifted to serving both hybrid and in-person audiences. This shift has led to advancements in mobile apps, such as lead capture, badge printing and scanning , and enhanced event apps. Innovations like artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) are also becoming more prevalent in event engagement technology. These technologies offer personalized content suggestions, boost attendee engagement, and create immersive experiences that transform attendees’ interactions with events. The rise of AI is making events more personalized and efficient, while virtual events are no longer limited to attendance but are also revolutionizing team-building and training. Flexibility is key in today’s event landscape, with attendees seeking options for fully virtual, hybrid, or in-person experiences. Reasons Why You Need an All-in-One Event Management Tool Event tech software has reshaped how events are planned, executed, and experienced. These all-in-one platforms serve as a centralized hub for event organizers, offering a wide range of features and functionalities tailored to various needs and preferences. From small business gatherings to large-scale conferences, event management tools drive innovation, efficiency, and enhanced attendee engagement. So you may ask, how exactly do I benefit from choosing such a platform? Let’s delve straight into that. Easier Event Management A key advantage of utilizing event management tools is the simplification of the entire event planning and execution process. These purpose-built platforms consolidate all the essential tasks, such as budgeting, scheduling, registration, attendee management, and communication, into one convenient location. In recent years, as mobile usage has grown, a digital membership card (or mobile event pass) has become a convenient, scannable pass for entry, perks, and member-only areas, while also helping track member activity. By centralizing these tasks, event planners can efficiently collaborate with their teams, ensuring everyone is on the same page. Real-time updates and seamless communication eliminate the need for endless back-and-forth exchanges, saving valuable time and enhancing productivity. Whether it’s a small company meeting or a large-scale conference, event management tools provide a comprehensive solution to streamline the event management process. Centralized Platform for Seamless Organization Organizing an event involves numerous moving parts, making it essential to have a centralized platform to manage all aspects efficiently. Event management tools, like InEvent or other event technology services, offer a centralized hub where event planners can oversee every aspect of their event. From creating event websites , managing registrations , and setting up schedules and agendas to tracking attendance , managing vendors and sponsors , and handling payments , everything can be seamlessly managed through a single interface. This consolidation simplifies the coordination of various tasks, eliminates the need for multiple tools and systems, and improves overall efficiency. With a centralized platform, event planners can focus on delivering exceptional experiences to attendees while ensuring everything runs smoothly behind the scenes. Effective Budget Tracking and Cost Management Managing event budgets and tracking expenses can be daunting without the right tools. Event technology software provides a comprehensive solution to maximize event ROI. With robust budgeting and tracking features , event planners can easily monitor every dollar spent and compare it against revenue. By visualizing registration data alongside expenditures, event planners gain valuable insights into their ROI and can make data-driven decisions to influence the success of their events. Additionally, event management tools enable event planners to automate financial processes, such as ticketing and payment collection, reducing the risk of errors and streamlining revenue management. With these cost management capabilities, event planners can optimize their event budgets and ensure every dollar is invested strategically. Enhancing Attendee Engagement Audience engagement is crucial to any event, whether before, during, or after. Event tech tools provide a range of features to boost attendee engagement at every stage. Through automated email campaigns , event planners can keep attendees excited and informed leading up to the event. Personalized communication and event updates ensure attendees remain engaged and anticipate the event’s value. During the event, interactive tools, such as live polling , Q&A sessions, and discussion forums, encourage active participation and create a sense of community among attendees. These engagement features facilitate meaningful interactions, increasing the likelihood that attendees take away valuable insights from the event. Even after the event concludes, event management tools enable event planners to continue the conversation, analyze attendee engagement, and customize outreach efforts for maximum response rates. Event planners can continuously improve and enhance future events by leveraging attendee engagement data. Data-Driven Decision Making In the world of event planning, making informed decisions based on data is crucial for success. Event management tools empower event planners to analyze attendee behavior, engagement metrics, and other relevant data in real time and at scale. Event planners can identify trends, measure event success, and make data-driven improvements by tracking these insights. Modern analytics and data infrastructure platforms, for example, Activeloop AI data analysis , make it easier to manage, index, and analyze large-scale attendee datasets, powering features like personalized recommendations, real-time dashboards, and advanced ML-driven segmentation. This data analysis enables event planners to enhance future events, tailoring them to meet the specific needs and preferences of attendees. Moreover, event management tools provide valuable post-event reporting and analytics , allowing event planners to evaluate the impact of their events and identify areas for further improvement. Event planners can continuously refine their strategies through data-driven decision-making and deliver exceptional event experiences. Streamlining Event Execution with Automation Event planners often wear multiple hats, juggling various tasks to ensure the success of an event. Event management tools come to the rescue by automating repetitive tasks, freeing up valuable time for event planners and their teams. By automating processes like registration, email communication, and data entry, event planners can focus on more strategic and creative aspects of event planning. Automated registration processes simplify attendee onboarding, reducing manual data entry and paperwork. Event management tools also enable event planners to automate email campaigns, ensuring timely and consistent communication with attendees. Automation also extends to on-site management, with features like automated check-in and badge printing , reducing wait times and enhancing the overall event experience. With automation, event planners can optimize their workflows, improve efficiency, and allocate more time to high-impact tasks. Presenting a Professional Event Experience The image and professionalism of an event significantly impact attendees’ perception and overall satisfaction. Event management tools are crucial in creating a seamless and professional event experience. By utilizing dedicated event platforms, event planners demonstrate their investment in delivering a comprehensive event experience. These platforms provide consistency in branding, messaging, and user experience, enhancing the overall event’s professionalism. Attendees interact with a cohesive event environment, ensuring a seamless and predictable experience. Moreover, event management tools empower event staff to focus on providing personalized touchpoints with attendees as the tools handle the behind-the-scenes details. By presenting a professional event experience, event management tools contribute to positive attendee impressions and foster long-term loyalty. Taking a Holistic Approach to Event Management Event management encompasses numerous aspects, from HR and accounting to registration, execution, and marketing. Event management tools consolidate these moving parts, providing a holistic approach to event planning. By centralizing all event-related tasks, event planners can delegate responsibilities more effectively, outsource specific components to vendors, and improve overall productivity. Technology has revolutionized event management, simplifying and streamlining processes to maximize event potential. Purpose-built event management tools, like InEvent, offer simplicity and comprehensiveness, enabling event planners to unlock the full potential of their events. The utilization of event management tools has revolutionized the event planning experience. These tools provide event planners with a centralized platform to streamline every aspect of event planning and execution. From simplifying event management to centralizing tasks, tracking costs, enhancing attendee engagement, and enabling data-driven decision-making, event management tools have become indispensable in delivering successful events. By automating tasks, providing a seamless attendee experience, and taking a holistic approach to event management, event planners can maximize the potential of their events and create unforgettable experiences for attendees. Embrace the power of event management tools and elevate your event planning to new heights. How To Choose the Right Event Technology Service for Your Needs Understanding the many advantages of all-in-one event tech software, picking a service that aligns perfectly with your unique event needs is crucial. Here’s a breakdown of key factors to keep in mind during your selection process: Ease of Use Look for software that is user-friendly. You don’t want to spend hours trying to figure out how to use it. The ideal software should have an intuitive interface that makes it easy for you and your team to manage events without a steep learning curve. Scalability Your chosen software should grow with your events. Whether you’re hosting small gatherings or large-scale conferences, the software must be capable of handling varying event sizes efficiently, ensuring a smooth experience as your needs evolve. Customization Options Every event is unique. Opt for software that offers extensive customization. This means being able to tailor features to suit your event’s specific theme, style, and requirements, from registration forms to ticketing options. Integrations Seamless integration with other tools is key. The software should work well with tools you already use, like email marketing platforms, CRM systems , or social media channels, to streamline your workflow and data management. Customer Support Good support can make a huge difference. Ensure that the software provider offers robust customer support , including quick response times, helpful guidance, and resources for troubleshooting, especially during critical moments. Event Requirements Consider the specific demands of your events. Do you need features for virtual participation, interactive sessions, or attendee tracking? Ensure the software caters to these specific functionalities to enhance the attendee experience. Request Demos or Trials Requesting demos or trials is an invaluable part of selecting the right event tech software. Here’s why it’s essential and how to make the most of it: Get a Real Feel of the Software : Demos and trials offer a hands-on experience. It’s one thing to read about features or watch tutorials, but using the software yourself gives you a clear sense of how it aligns with your needs. Pay attention to how intuitive and user-friendly the interface is. Test Specific Features : Use this opportunity to test out specific features that are critical to your events. If you’re keen on live polling, virtual networking, or real-time analytics, see how these functionalities work in action. Make a list of must-have features and check them off during the demo. Assess Customization and Scalability : While you’re trying out the software, evaluate how easily it can be customized to fit your brand and event style. Also, consider if the software can handle different event sizes and types, ensuring it’s a solution that can grow with you. Evaluate Customer Support : During your trial period, take note of the responsiveness and helpfulness of customer support. his could include their customer service function , availability, the resources they provide, and how effectively they address any questions or issues you encounter. Gather Team Feedback : If possible, involve your team in the trial process. Their insights can be invaluable, as different team members might use various aspects of the software. Collecting their feedback ensures you choose a solution that works well for everyone involved. Compare and Contrast : If you’re trialing multiple options, compare them to see which best meets your needs. Look beyond just the features – consider aspects like ease of use, integration capabilities, and overall user experience. Make Informed Decisions : Ultimately, demos and trials empower you to make an informed decision. They help you understand what the software does and how it can enhance your event management process and attendee experience. Remember, the goal of a demo or trial isn’t just to see if the software works but to ensure it works for you and your specific event requirements. By carefully assessing your needs and considering these factors, you can choose the right event management tool that aligns with your event objectives and enhances your overall event management experience. Budget and long-term goals Lastly, align your choice with your financial plan and future aspirations. While affordability is important, consider the software’s long-term benefits and ROI. title: From Alignment to Execution: Strengthening Our Partner Ecosystem for the Next Phase of Growth
summary: Broadcom is strengthening its partner ecosystem to help customers scale VMware Cloud Foundation and modern private cloud environments for AI and enterprise workloads
body_text: A Year of Progress and a Shift to Execution When I stepped into this role a year ago, much of our time with partners was focused on portfolio changes and clarifying what it meant to operate within the new model. Those were necessary conversations as we reset the foundation of Broadcom’s partner ecosystem. Today, our conversations are about scaling execution with a focus around helping customers deliver outcomes. Partners are now focused on scaling the capabilities required to meet accelerating demand for modern private cloud. That means designing and deploying VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) environments at scale, helping customers solve real business challenges, and supporting the next wave of workloads, from traditional applications to containerized and AI-driven environments. Building a Partner Ecosystem Designed for Outcomes We have sharpened our focus on a partner ecosystem that is aligned, highly capable, and invested in customer success. We simplified partner motions and strengthened alignment across sales, technical teams, and operations to create a more effective model. This was about improving execution and ensuring that partners who engage are positioned to deliver meaningful outcomes for customers. The foundation is now in place. What Partners Can Expect in 2026 As we move forward, our priorities are clear: value, outcomes, and adoption. Demand for modern private cloud continues to grow, and in the Commercial segment we recognize the need for flexibility. In light of broader market dynamics, including server cost pressures and overall cost-to-deploy, we are rebalancing our approach to ensure partners can meet customers where they are. This includes a renewed focus on VMware vSphere Foundation (VVF) as an important entry point for Commercial customers, enabling them to modernize their infrastructure, optimize existing investments, and take a more incremental path toward full VCF adoption over time. Success will be defined by partners who can guide customers along this journey, starting with the right foundation, then expanding into areas like automation, Kubernetes, software-defined storage, and private AI as their customer's needs evolve. In 2026, we are guiding partners to: Strengthen technical and services capabilities to support both VVF-led entry points and full VCF adoption Lead customers through a phased modernization journey, aligned to cost, complexity, and business priorities Deliver predictable, repeatable outcomes through proven architectures and services Drive adoption of VCF and its expanding capabilities, including storage, networking, security, and Kubernetes, at the right pace for each customer Partners who can lead customers up this value curve will deepen their strategic relevance and drive long-term growth. Scaling Capability Through Enablement and Experience To support this shift, Broadcom is making targeted investments in partner enablement. We are expanding the Knights program to build deep technical expertise, scaling our Activation events for both sales and technical audiences, and introducing more hands-on experiences such as VCF Experience Days to accelerate customer adoption. At the same time, we are aligning sales plays around real customer priorities, storage optimization, networking, security, and workload modernization, while enabling partners to expand into areas like competitive displacement and workload repatriation over time. We are also seeing momentum in partner-led customer success stories. Amplifying these outcomes, through co-authored content and industry engagement, will be a key part of scaling the ecosystem’s impact. Navigating Today’s Environment and Where We Are Focused Customers are operating in a dynamic environment, including cost pressures driven by factors like server market shifts and memory pricing. Our focus is helping partners guide customers through this with practical, high-impact solutions. This includes: Leveraging memory tiering to optimize infrastructure efficiency Driving greater utilization of existing investments in vSAN, VKS, and core platform capabilities Expanding focus on lateral movement security with vDefend to provide the visibility and protection customers need Supporting containerized workloads and private cloud-based AI initiatives These are immediate, actionable opportunities for partners to deliver value while helping customers manage cost and complexity. A More Focused, More Impactful Ecosystem We will continue to focus on what is working, where partners are winning, and how customer success translates into sustained growth. Private cloud is a platform strategy requiring thoughtful planning, phased adoption, and continuous optimization. That is why we are prioritizing partners who bring deep expertise and a commitment to delivering outcomes across the entire customer lifecycle. This evolution is about creating: More value per partner Better outcomes per customer Durable, long-term growth across the ecosystem The opportunity ahead is significant, and together with our partners, we are well positioned to lead it. About the Author About the Author Brian Moats Senior Vice President, Global Commercial Sales and Partners, Broadcom

title: MATTHEWS INTERNATIONAL ANNOUNCES PARTIAL REDEMPTION OF PREFERRED EQUITY INTEREST IN PROPELIS

body_text: PITTSBURGH , May 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Matthews International Corporation (NASDAQ GSM: MATW) today announced receipt of $28 million of proceeds for the partial redemption of its preferred equity interest in Propelis. In discussing this redemption, Joseph C. Bartolacci, President and Chief Executive Officer, stated: "The Propelis joint venture has continued to perform in line with our expectations since the merger of our SGK Brand Solutions business with SGS & Co. one year ago. This redemption is further evidence of the business' ability to continue to grow adjusted EBITDA, capture synergies, and ultimately return value to its shareholders." About Matthews International Corporation Matthews International Corporation operates through two core global businesses – Industrial Technologies and Memorialization. Both are focused on driving operational efficiency and long-term growth through continuous innovation and strategic expansion. The Industrial Technologies segment evolved from our original marking business, which today is a leading global innovator committed to empowering visionaries to transform industries through the application of precision technologies and intelligent processes. The Memorialization segment is a leading provider of memorialization products, including memorials, caskets and cremation and incineration equipment, primarily to cemetery and funeral home customers that help families move from grief to remembrance. In addition, the Company also has a significant investment in Propelis, a brand solutions business formed through the merger of SGK and SGS & Co. Propelis delivers integrated solutions including brand creative, packaging, print solutions, branded environments, and content production. Matthews International has over 4,300 employees in 15 countries on four continents that are committed to delivering the highest quality products and services.
